I have farmed these fields in Quzhou for more than fifty years. I am seventy now, and while my legs are not as strong as they once were, I still know every mu of my land. My household has 12 mu of good flat soil on the North China Plain, and I see no reason to gamble with new crops at my age. This year, just like last year and the year before, I will grow winter wheat and summer maize in a double crop. The wheat went into the ground last October after the rains, and it is greening up now. As soon as we harvest it in early June, I will plant the maize.

I buy improved wheat seed—Jimai 22—from the village supply store because it is reliable and resists lodging. For the summer maize I use Denghai 605 hybrid seed. It costs more than keeping my own grain, but the yield is higher and the traders at the market pay a better price for hybrid corn. For the wheat field I still do rotary tillage in the autumn to break up the stubble, but for maize I stopped ploughing years ago; there is no time between wheat harvest and maize sowing, and at my age no-tillage saves my back and lets me keep up with the season.

For fertilizer, I follow what the shopkeeper recommends and what my neighbors use. I spread compound fertilizer as a basal dose and topdress with urea when the crops are growing. For wheat I put down about 15 kg of nitrogen, 10 kg of phosphate, and 4 kg of potash per mu. For maize the season is shorter, so I use about 11 kg nitrogen, 3 kg phosphate, and 3 kg potash per mu.

Water is precious and electricity for the pump is expensive, so I count every irrigation. I will water the wheat four times: once before winter so the roots do not freeze, and three more times in spring when the ears are filling. The maize usually gets two good irrigations in July and August if the summer rains fall short. I also watch the fields for pests. I normally need to spray four times for wheat and three times for maize—herbicide, insecticide, and a little fungicide—to keep the leaves healthy and the grains full.

If the weather is kind and there is no big flood or drought, I expect about 500 kg of wheat per mu and 550 kg of maize per mu. That will be enough for our family flour and to sell the surplus to the grain station.
